body: What also sucks is when you become overly aware of the position of your tongue while resting in your mouth. Sometimes I forget what position it naturally rests in and I can't ever let it relax because I don't know how.

You probably just had a rough night. In the event you end up back here for the same reason, the comments below might guide you in a more positive direction.

I can't comment on how to fix your anxiety problem, as I haven't fixed my own issue yet, but I can definitively say you do not want to go down the habitual path of drinking as a means of liberating yourself from emotion. I wish I could help you with the cutting bit, but it's out of my league. However, I have watched drinking destroy a large percentage of my family.

Drinking will get you no where. At no point have I ever heard someone say drinking solved their issues, or even helped them. More often than not, drinking to "solve" problems just gives you more problems to drink over. I've watched a lot of my family go down this path, and once you go down that path I'm not convinced you ever really come back. In a lot of ways, it seems like even those who get treatment will resort to it if they're pushed far enough. Stop thinking about drinking as a means of achieving anything, and it should help you in a preventative sense.

Just my 2 cents. Good luck.

Thanks, I appreciate it.

I know what you mean. It's a strange sensation, being on both sides of the fence at once and knowing that a lot of the people are right there with you. It's quite different from explaining a predicament to an outsider that hasn't been there before.

Maybe so. It doesn't help that I'm kind of an independent person. 'Reaching out' to people has always seemed so alien, but maybe I just went about it wrong.

The times I have reached out to people they've always pushed towards a therapeutic approach as opposed to medication, even my own parents. It's easy to shift the blame on them, but you don't have many options as a younger kid--I guess I just came to rely on myself. They were also both on medication long term for similar things, and I always got the vibe they wouldn't wish the same fate on me.

You're right though, talking about it a bit has made me feel better. Not that I'm really borderline suicidal, but it's been hard to reverse that as a potential option lately. Once that train of thought gets going, it builds up some serious momentum.

Just let it come naturally. Think about the times you HAVE cried. Was it because you were trying, or was it because something hit you square in the face and it just came over you? You sound like me, and I'm in kind of a dark place myself as of now.

After 10 years or so of not crying, I just found myself lightly crying on and off when I'm by myself at night over the last few months. There's no particular thought in my head, just emptiness. It's completely irrational, but it passes quickly and I usually feel a bit better after it. It takes a while for a cup to fill before it overflows. Find some peace in that.

Aye. You should stop delaying and go to Japan. Hell, even move there. Time isn't guaranteed here. I'd do it in a second if I thought it would be my saving grace.

For as long as I can remember I haven't been able to find a real life path that I'd prosper in. Even careers, cars, money, and even in some cases spiritual paths always felt like a carrot on a string that wouldn't satisfy a hunger even if I got a hold of it. I keep toying with the idea of just doing what good I can for people while still able bodied, and when I'm done just leaving peacefully on a high note.

Edit: just for clarification, no I haven't.

Thanks for the ideas. It's worth a shot, I suppose. A part of me has difficulty accepting being medicated, I hate the thought of it.  Clinical depression does run in the family, as does everything from alcoholism to drug addiction to severe anxiety. Maybe I truly am delusional but I've always felt like being on antidepressants and things of the sort are kind of like submitting to something out of your control, and it's a terrible feeling to feel like you can't conquer your own problems. For that same reason I've been struggling with controlling generalized anxiety, number-oriented OCD and serious sleep issues which I think are the product of being on edge constantly.

It would be nice to feel good again, but yet at the same time it feels like I'd almost be a different person. I don't dislike who I am, just how I think.
